# MLB DAILY BRIEFING | April 29, 2026

## HEADLINE RESULTS

What a night of dominant pitching and offensive explosions! The Brewers absolutely pummeled Arizona 13-2 at American Family Field, using classic small ball to manufacture runs while waiting for injured sluggers Jackson Chourio and Andrew Vaughn to return. Meanwhile, the Mets finally gave their frustrated home fans something to cheer about with an 8-0 shutout of Washington at Citi Field, featuring homers from Bo Bichette and Juan Soto.

And don't sleep on that Cardinals-Pirates slugfest in Pittsburgh — St. Louis outlasted the Bucs 11-7 in a game that saw 25 combined hits and five home runs.

## STANDINGS WATCH

The NL Central is absolutely loaded right now. Cincinnati sits atop the division at 19-10, but the Cubs are breathing down their necks just one game back at 19-12. The Cardinals' big win moves them to 16-13, while Milwaukee and Pittsburgh are both hovering around .533. This could be a four-team race deep into summer.

Over in the AL East, the Yankees are flexing at 20-11, but Tampa Bay at 18-12 is only a game and a half behind — that's a divisional battle worth watching.

## STORYLINE OF THE DAY

**The Strikeout Kings Emerge**

Three pitchers set new season highs on the same night — and we're talking significant jumps. Clay Holmes punched out 11 in the Mets' shutout, nearly doubling his previous 2026 best of five. Kyle Leahy fanned 11 for St. Louis, up from just six. Even Chad Patrick jumped from four to eight for Milwaukee. When that many arms suddenly find another gear simultaneously, you have to wonder if something's in the air — or if hitters are just getting that much more vulnerable as we approach May.
